title: Read which fields a captured message carries

blocks.text: Support pastes messages captured on hex-ASCII links into tickets. The first questions are always the same: which fields does the sender say it sent, and where do they begin? Today someone answers them with a pencil, and gets them wrong about once a week.

`DumpReader` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/DumpReader.java` takes one capture, from the MTI on, exactly as the link carried it. Its constructor and `mti()` already work. Write the three methods marked `TODO`:

items: `bit(from, n)`, which the other two use;
`fields()`, every field the capture says is present, in ascending order;
`dataStart()`, the index in the capture where the first field's characters begin.

blocks.text: The tool reads at most two bitmaps. A capture that announces a third one must not be reported as something it isn't: `fields()` refuses it with an `IllegalArgumentException`.

cases.says: a capture with one bitmap gives its MTI, every field its bitmap marks, in ascending order, and the index where the fields begin
a capture with two bitmaps lists the fields of both, and the bit that announces the second bitmap is not listed as a field
when a second bitmap follows the first, the fields begin after it, not after the first
a capture whose second bitmap announces a third one is refused, never read as carrying field 65

origin.section: 2.3. Bit 1 Announces a Second Bitmap, So It Is Never a Field

concepts: Bit 65 announces a tertiary bitmap the way bit 1 announces the secondary one, so field 65 carries no data.
Bit 1 announces a secondary bitmap for fields 65 to 128, which comes before the first field; bit 1 itself is not a field.
Bit n of a bitmap says field n is present, counted from 1 at the most significant bit of the first byte.
